description.short: Few songs in 2024 hit a high note quite like Billie Eilish’s “BIRDS OF A FEATHER.”
description.standard: Few songs in 2024 resonated quite like Billie Eilish’s “BIRDS OF A FEATHER,” a warm, weightless, pan-genre pop tune that felt right for any mood or circumstance this year. It’s Eilish’s most airy and accessible music to date, but just as importantly, it represented real growth: It’s the sound of the (now two-time) Apple Music Artist of the Year purely herself, pushing her voice and putting herself out there like never before. “It’s the highest I’ve ever belted in my life,” she told Apple Music Radio’s Zane Lowe of the song’s soaring finish. “I was alone in the dark, thinking, ‘You know what? I’m going to try something.’ And I literally just kept going higher and higher. This is a girl who could not belt until I was literally 18. I couldn’t physically do it. So I’m so proud of that. I remember coming home and being like, ‘Mom! Listen!’”

description.short: Sabrina Carpenter’s strong “Espresso” was just a first taste of her dominant year.
description.standard: A-List Pop is your weekly guide to what’s on top in pop music—and 2024 was undeniably the year of Sabrina Carpenter. The 25-year-old singer-songwriter’s sixth studio album Short n’ Sweet parked itself on top of the Apple Music charts for the majority of 2024, while the singles “Espresso,” “Please Please Please,” and “Taste” all became viral anthems, leaving their mark on culture and in our heads. Carpenter’s music is brutally honest, funny, and, most importantly, catchy. “There really are no rules to the things you say,” she told Zane Lowe about the songwriting process. “You’re just like, what sounds awesome? What feels awesome? And what gets the story across, whatever story that is?” And that’s that me espresso.

description.short: The tracks that defined this most electric of years.
description.standard: Looking back, 2024 has been a year of high stakes—everything felt electrified. Consider the vivid sounds (and vivid green) of Charli’s Brat Summer, or the sulfurous crackle of Kendrick’s “Not Like Us.” We were witness to a bracing new wave of pop ushered in by Sabrina Carpenter and Chappell Roan, not to mention the breathtaking rise of FloyyMenor, Cris MJ, and Chilean urbano. There was a real charge to the sing-or-die anthemics of crooners like Benson Boone and Teddy Swims, just as there was a genuine thrill in seeing Beyoncé, Shaboozey, and Post Malone leave their mark on country music. Everything felt new and sounded like it mattered—and music was better for it.

description.short: Music’s biggest and brightest songs—as you’ve never heard them before.
description.standard: Ever wish you could get that feeling of hearing your favorite song for the first time all over again? No problem. Thanks to Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos, now on Apple Music, you can be fully immersed in the songs you love, as if you’ve stepped inside of them. The vocals you harmonize with, the beats you move to: All of it can feel real enough to touch, like you’re at the center of it all. It’s a three-dimensional listening experience where sound comes from around and above you. Handmade by our editors, this playlist showcases some of music’s biggest and brightest songs as you’ve never heard them before. There’s no turning back from here.

description.short: Charli xcx’s “Apple” music helped make 2024 so BRAT.
description.standard: Social media hasn’t just changed how we communicate, but also what we listen to and how we hear it. With that, here’s our playlist of tracks that made the leap from your social channels into the broader cultural stream in 2024. Leading the conversation is Charli xcx’s “Apple,” just one of the tracks that made BRAT, a neon-green omnipresence for much of the year. “I am prepared in ways for what’s happening right now in terms of the pace of things and also in terms of my level of engagement with reality versus fantasy,” she told Apple Music’s Zane Lowe of her sixth album’s dominance. And that’s “so Julia” of her.

description.short: Billie Eilish ate the world for “LUNCH” in 2024.
description.standard: ALT CTRL is home to the latest and greatest in alternative music. Here, it’s as much an attitude as a sound—music that keeps things a little left of center and rough around the edges. Ending the year with a bang is Billie Eilish’s “LUNCH,” the orally pleasing, sapphic single from her third album HIT ME HARD AND SOFT. “One of the verses was written after a conversation I had with a friend and they were telling me about this complete animal magnetism they were feeling. And I was like, ‘Ooh, I’m going to pretend to be them for a second and just write…and I’m gonna throw some jokes in there,’” Eilish told Apple Music’s Zane Lowe of the song’s construction. “When you start to embrace cringe, you’re so much happier. You have so much more fun.”
